name: 静水门
Still Water Gate
before: 后千里穿出最后一层蜃气，海忽然平了：没有浪，没有涌，船尾划开的水痕不往两边散，像犁过一块不会合拢的豆腐。三百盏灯笼倒映在水里，一盏不晃，看上去成了六百盏。前方一道白礁像矮墙，墙后是一片草地，岸上站着一排归墟亡兵，脸上平平的，什么都没有，像被海水磨了一百年的石头。小桨趴在船头听了半天：「听不见浪。」

Houqianli slips out of the last veil of mirage and the sea goes suddenly flat: no waves, no swell, and the wake behind the stern does not spread, like a plough furrow through bean curd that never closes. The three hundred lanterns hang in the water without a tremor, so there seem to be six hundred. Ahead a white reef runs like a low wall with grassland behind it, and on the shore stands a line of the Ruins' dead soldiers. Their faces are flat and blank, like stones the sea has worn for a hundred years. Xiaojiang lies in the bow listening for a long while. 'I can't hear any waves.'
after: 亡兵一个接一个倒退着走进水里，没起一圈涟漪。岸上立着一块老碑，字是古篆：「归墟。来者勿留。」碑脚下另有一行新些的刻字，刀口还发白：「千里号过此。」龚墨斗摸着刀口说，刻字的人手很稳，刻完还把石屑吹干净了。

One by one the dead soldiers walk backwards into the water without raising a single ripple. An old stele stands on the shore in ancient seal script: 'The Return Ruins. Who comes, do not stay.' Lower down, a newer line, the cuts still pale: 'The Qianli passed here.' Gong Modou runs a thumb along the strokes. Whoever carved it had a steady hand, he says, and blew the dust away when they were done.

name: 千桨原
Field of Oars
before: 草原上插满了船桨，几百根，直挺挺地竖着，像一片长歪了的芦苇。没有一丝风，桨杆却吱吱地响。三路守墟人在桨林里扎营：亡兵守着桨，亡弓蹲在桨后，亡骑绕着外圈走。谁伸手碰一根桨，他们就把它拔出来，换个地方重新插好。

Oars stand upright all over the grassland, hundreds of them, like a reed bed grown crooked. There is not a breath of wind, yet the shafts creak. Three columns of Ruin-keepers camp among them: dead soldiers guard the oars, dead archers crouch behind them, dead riders circle the edge. Touch an oar and they pull it out and plant it again somewhere else.
after: 守墟人退了。龚墨斗挨根看过去：桨上刻着各式各样的船号，有的是百年前的样子，这里是到了归墟的船放下桨的地方。阿汐在里头找到一根，桨叶上一道潮刻，旁边一个「许」字。她把手按在刻痕上：「爹把桨放下了。」

The keepers fall back. Gong Modou goes from oar to oar: every one is carved with a ship's mark, some in styles a century old. This is where ships that reached the Ruins laid down their oars. Axi finds one with a tide notch cut into the blade and the character Xu beside it. She lays her palm on the notch. 'Father put down his oar.'

name: 挂袋树
Satchel Tree
before: 野地里一棵枯树，白得像骨头，最高的枝上挂着一只帆布信袋，鼓鼓囊囊。几个亡骑绕着树一圈圈地走。树下坐着个瘦老头，戴一顶大斗笠，啃着一块干饼，一点也不急。他左脚的草鞋糊满黄沙，右脚的糊满红泥，裤脚上结着一圈盐霜。见你们过来，他拍拍饼渣：「不急，我晚惯了。劳驾，帮我把袋子够下来。」

A dead tree stands alone in the open, white as bone, and from its highest branch hangs a canvas letter satchel, stuffed full. A few dead riders circle the trunk, round and round. Beneath it sits a thin old man in a broad straw hat, chewing a dry flatbread, in no hurry at all. His left sandal is caked with yellow sand, his right with red mud, and his trouser cuffs are crusted with salt. He brushes off the crumbs as you come up. 'No rush. I'm used to being late. Would you mind getting my bag down?'
after: 亡骑散了，信袋取了下来。老头自称晏伯，是个信客，专送「寄给回不来的人」的信。他一封封数过，一封不少，抬头看了阿汐一眼：「许领港家的闺女吧？看海先看月亮，跟你爹一个样。」阿汐一愣，他已经笑着系好了袋口：「送信的嘛，谁家的脸都认得几张。」

The riders scatter and the satchel comes down. The old man calls himself Old Yan, a letter carrier who delivers 'letters to people who don't come back'. He counts them one by one, none missing, then glances up at Axi. 'You'll be Pilot Xu's girl. Looks at the moon before she looks at the sea, just like her father.' Axi starts, but he is already tying the bag shut with a smile. 'A letter carrier knows a face or two from every house.'

name: 拾遗栈
Flotsam Inn
before: 野地上一座客栈，墙是船板，顶是旧帆，门匾是半截舵。这是漂到归墟的人歇脚的地方，如今被一伙捞客占了：海上漂来什么，他们捞什么，鞋子、扣子、信，连死人的金牙都拿去卖。为了吓人，他们戴着没鼻子没眼的白面具，冒充守墟人；楼上的弓手一样戴着面具，射得倒是真准。

An inn stands in the open, walls of ship's planking, roof of old sail, and half a rudder for a signboard. It is where those who drift into the Ruins come to rest, and a gang of salvagers has taken it. Whatever the sea brings, they fish out and sell: shoes, buttons, letters, even dead men's gold teeth. To frighten people they wear white masks with no nose or eyes and pass themselves off as Ruin-keepers. The archers upstairs are masked too, and their aim is real enough.
after: 捞客被赶了出去，面具扔了一地，漂客们回了栈。晏伯在柜台上把信摊开分拣，挑出一封发黄的，递给阿汐：「许潮生收，母字。丁未年冬天寄的，我揣了十年，没追上他。你们腿快，捎一程。」说完戴上斗笠，一个人往东去了：「顺路，我先走一步。」

The salvagers are thrown out, masks littering the floor, and the castaways move back in. Old Yan spreads his letters on the counter to sort them, picks out a yellowed one and hands it to Axi. 'To Xu Chaosheng, from his mother. Sent the winter of the Dingwei year. I've carried it ten years and never caught up with him. Your legs are quicker than mine. Take it the rest of the way.' Then he puts on his hat and sets off east alone. 'It's on my way. I'll go on ahead.'
first: 楼上抄出捞客囤的三十几双不配对的鞋、一桶铜扣子、四十斤咸鱼、两坛淡水，还有一箱撬下来的船钉，每根都擦得锃亮，准备论斤卖。

Upstairs you seize the salvagers' hoard: thirty-odd unmatched shoes, a bucket of brass buttons, forty jin of salt fish, two jars of fresh water, and a crate of prised-out ship's nails, every one polished bright to be sold by weight.
pass: 每次路过，漂客们都端出一锅鱼汤，再从那堆鞋里替你们挑几双合脚的，刷得干干净净：「鞋嘛，就该接着走路。」
Each time you pass, the castaways bring out a pot of fish soup and pick a few pairs from the shoe pile that fit your feet, scrubbed clean. 'Shoes are meant to keep walking.'

name: 停漏庵
Stopped Clock Hermitage
before: 一座茅草小庵，门口堆着一座小山，全是砸碎的漏壶、沙漏、日晷和潮尺。庵里住着「静海会」的人，他们说归墟的海不动，时辰也就停了，留着计时的东西是罪过。会众披着灰布，拿木杖守住庵门，看见你们船上的更漏，嚷着要「替你们解脱」。会首是个泉州来的老钟匠，砸得最狠。

Outside a little thatched hermitage rises a heap of smashed water clocks, hourglasses, sundials and tide rods. The Still Sea Society lives here. The sea of the Ruins does not move, they say, so time has stopped, and keeping anything that measures it is a sin. Draped in grey cloth, the faithful bar the gate with staves and, spotting the watch clock on your ship, cry out to 'set you free'. Their leader is an old clockmaker from Quanzhou, and he smashes hardest of all.
after: 会众散了。阿汐在礁上守了半天，划下两道刻痕：水涨了一尺多，又慢慢退了下去。「有潮。小，可是有。」她一回头，看见庵墙上一行炭笔旧字：「潮小一尺，人勿慌。许。」老钟匠盯着那行字看了很久，蹲下去，捡起一只摔扁的漏壶。

The faithful scatter. Axi keeps watch on the reef for half a day and scratches two marks: the water rises a foot and more, then slowly falls back. 'There's a tide. Small, but it's there.' Turning, she sees an old line in charcoal on the hermitage wall: 'The tide is only a foot. Do not panic. Xu.' The old clockmaker stares at it a long time, then crouches and picks up a flattened water clock.

name: 扫沙道
Swept Sand Path
before: 野地里一条白沙小路，扫得干干净净，一片落叶都没有，弯弯曲曲往北去。路口驻着一营守墟人，亡兵、亡弓、亡骑都有，见人就往回赶。打到最后，别的守墟人都退进了水里，只剩一个不走：他捡起一把椰叶扫帚，转过身，接着扫地。他手腕上拴着一只铜铃，绿得发黑。

A little path of white sand winds north through the open land, swept so clean there is not a single leaf on it. A camp of Ruin-keepers holds its mouth, soldiers, archers and riders, turning back anyone who comes. When the fight is over the rest retreat into the water, all but one. He picks up a broom of palm fronds, turns his back, and goes on sweeping. A copper bell is tied at his wrist, green almost to black.
after: 他不理你们，一下一下地扫。铜铃里头刻着「茶·十七」，是马帮的牲口号。阿汐在路边捡起一枚贝壳，壳上一道刻痕，跟千桨原那根桨上的一模一样；每隔一百步就有一枚，一路往北。爹走过这条路。你们跟在扫地人后面走。

He ignores you and sweeps, stroke by stroke. Inside his bell is engraved 'Tea, Seventeen': a caravan mule's number. By the path Axi picks up a shell with a notch cut in it, the same as the one on the oar in the field. There is one every hundred paces, all the way north. Father walked this path. You fall in behind the sweeper.

name: 椰蟹林
Robber Crab Grove
before: 一片椰林，树底下躺满了啃开的椰壳。林子里驻着一队亡兵，一动不动地站着，站久了，椰子蟹把他们当成了树，一只只顺着腿往上爬。那蟹有狗那么大，钳子夹得开椰子，专偷亮东西。你们船上的铜锅刚卸下岸，一转眼就被拖走了一只。

A coconut grove, the ground beneath strewn with gnawed husks. A squad of dead soldiers stands motionless among the trees, and they have stood so long that the robber crabs take them for trunks and climb their legs. The crabs are the size of dogs, with claws that crack coconuts, and they steal anything that shines. Your ship's copper pots have barely touched the sand when one is dragged away.
after: 亡兵散了，铜锅在蟹洞里找着了，洞里还堆着勺子、扣子、半截烟杆，和一只铜测深锤。锤底凿着凹坑，坑里抹的牛油早已发硬，粘着一层粉红的碎屑。阿汐说这是领港的老法子：锤底抹油，落到海底，提上来一看，就知道底是泥、是沙还是礁。「爹在这儿量过，底下是珊瑚。」

The soldiers scatter and the pot turns up in a crab hole, along with spoons, buttons, half a pipe stem, and a brass sounding lead. Its base is hollowed out, the tallow packed in it long gone hard and stuck with pink grit. It's the old pilots' trick, Axi says: grease the bottom of the lead, let it touch the seabed, pull it up and you know whether the bottom is mud, sand or reef. 'Father sounded here. The bottom is coral.'

name: 湿蹄滩
Wet Hoof Strand
before: 黄昏，海滩上响起了马蹄声。一队亡骑骑着灰马沿着水边跑过来，马蹄印一踩下去就灌满了水，一路亮晶晶的。滩上一户渔家把船倒扣过来当屋子，一家五口缩在船底下，从板缝里往外看。他们说这队骑兵每天黄昏都来跑一趟，跑完就进海，一天也不落。

At dusk hoofbeats sound along the beach. A troop of dead riders comes galloping on grey horses at the water's edge, each hoofprint filling with water the moment it is made, a glittering trail behind them. A fishing family has turned their boat upside down for a house, and all five of them huddle beneath it, peering through the cracks. The riders come every evening, they say, run the length of the beach, then ride into the sea. They have never missed a day.
after: 亡骑败了，蹄印一路通进海里，停在两道白礁之间的一个豁口前。渔老汉说那是南礁门，外头的船只能从这儿进来，还得赶大潮。十年前的秋天，一溜大船就是从这里一条接一条进来的，船头站着一个人，拿泉州话一声一声地报水深。阿汐说：「是我爹。」

The riders are beaten, and their hoofprints lead into the sea and stop before a gap between two white reefs. The South Reef Gate, the old fisherman calls it: ships from outside can only come in through there, and only on a spring tide. Ten years ago in autumn a string of big ships came through, one after another, and a man stood in the bow calling the depths in the Quanzhou tongue. 'That was my father,' Axi says.

name: 鲸骨村
Whalebone Village
before: 野地里一座村子，屋架全是鲸鱼的肋骨，一根根弯成拱，上面盖着草席。村里住着几十户漂客，可这几天一大营守墟人住了进来：亡兵睡在骨屋里，亡弓坐在骨梁上，亡骑把马拴在鲸鱼的下巴骨上。他们什么也不干，就是住着，村里人只好抱着孩子睡在外头的草地上。

A village stands in the open, every house framed with whale ribs bent into arches and roofed with grass mats. A few dozen castaway families live here, but for days now a large camp of Ruin-keepers has moved in: soldiers sleep in the bone houses, archers sit on the bone beams, riders tether their horses to a whale's jaw. They do nothing at all, they just live there, and the villagers sleep out on the grass with their children in their arms.
after: 守墟人走了，村里人搬回了骨屋。一群孩子围着你们看，阿汐随口问了一句今天几时涨潮，一个光脚丫头张嘴就背：「月上头，水上岸；月落西，水回家；初一十五潮最大。」阿汐愣住了：这是她爹教她的歌，一字不差。丫头说是黑脸的许先生教的：「学会了，就不怕海。」

The keepers leave and the villagers move back into their bone houses. A crowd of children gathers to stare at you. Axi asks idly when the tide comes in today, and a barefoot girl rattles off: 'Moon overhead, water on the shore; moon in the west, water goes home; new moon and full, the tide is at its fullest.' Axi stops short. It is the song her father taught her, word for word. A dark-faced Teacher Xu taught them, the girl says. 'He said once you know it, you won't be afraid of the sea.'

name: 搓绳岗
Rope Twister's Rise
before: 野地里一座小岗，岗上绕着一座小山似的麻绳，一圈压一圈。搓绳的是个白胡子老头，人称量海翁，他说归墟没有底，搓了十年绳，要放下去量一量。一队亡弓占了岗子，拿火箭射那堆绳，烧一截，老头就扑上去拿身子压灭一截，胡子都燎焦了半边。

On a low rise sits a mountain of hemp rope, coil upon coil. The man twisting it is a white-bearded old fellow called the Sea Measurer. The Ruins have no bottom, he says, and he has spent ten years making rope to lower down and find out. A squad of dead archers has taken the rise and is shooting fire arrows into the pile. Every time a stretch catches, the old man throws himself on it to smother it, and half his beard is singed.
after: 亡弓退了。老头说他放下去两千多丈，还没碰着底。阿汐翻开潮信簿，爹在一页上写着：「此去南百里，海底有沟，深过高山，非无底也。」海沟是海底裂开的一道深槽，最深处，把天下最高的山整座放进去，山顶也露不出水面。量海翁听完，抹了把脸：「那我再搓一千丈。」

The archers fall back. The old man says he has let down more than two thousand zhang of line and never touched bottom. Axi opens the tide book: on one page her father wrote, 'A hundred li south, a trench in the seabed, deeper than mountains are high. Not bottomless.' A trench is a deep gash in the sea floor; at its deepest, you could drop the tallest mountain in the world into it and its peak would not break the surface. The Sea Measurer wipes his face. 'Then I'll twist another thousand.'

name: 烧灰滩
Lime Kiln Beach
before: 海滩上一座土窑冒着白烟，一个老阿婆从礁上撬下死珊瑚，背回来烧石灰，抹船缝、刷墙都用得上。一队亡兵站在礁上，不许她撬，见她背篓里有珊瑚，就把整篓倒回海里。老阿婆气得拿铁铲敲他们的胫甲，敲得当当响：「死的！我撬的是死的！」

A clay kiln smokes white on the beach. An old woman prises dead coral off the reef and carries it back to burn for lime, good for caulking seams and whitewashing walls. A squad of dead soldiers stands on the reef and will not let her, and whenever they see coral in her basket they tip the lot back into the sea. Furious, she bangs their greaves with her iron shovel until they ring. 'It's dead! I only take the dead stuff!'
after: 亡兵退了。老阿婆说她年轻时潜过水：浅水里的珊瑚是活的，五颜六色；越往深处越是死珊瑚，一层压一层，压到最底下是黑石头。「是底下的山在沉，珊瑚一辈一辈往上长，山沉没了，就剩这一圈礁。」阿汐翻开潮信簿，爹在一页上画了个圈：「归墟如环，中是旧山。」

The soldiers retreat. The old woman says she dived as a girl: in the shallows the coral is alive and every colour; deeper down it is all dead coral, layer on layer, and at the very bottom black rock. 'The mountain underneath is sinking, and the coral grows up and up, generation after generation. The mountain goes under, and only the ring of reef is left.' Axi opens the tide book. On one page her father drew a circle: 'The Ruins are a ring. In the middle, an old mountain.'

name: 漂瓶湾
Bottle Bay
before: 一道海湾里堆满了漂来的瓶子，陶的、瓷的、竹筒的，瓶口都塞着东西。漂客说海上的流在这里打旋，四面八方漂来的东西都转进湾里，出不去。一伙亡弓守着瓶堆，谁捡一只就射谁的手。湾边住着个识字的漂客，偷偷替人念瓶里的字，念一封，挨一箭。

A bay is heaped with bottles washed in from the sea, clay, porcelain, bamboo, every mouth stoppered. The currents swirl here, the castaways say, and whatever floats in from every quarter turns into the bay and never gets out. A band of dead archers guards the pile and shoots the hand of anyone who picks one up. A castaway who can read lives at the bay's edge and secretly reads the messages aloud for people, one arrow per letter.
after: 亡弓退了。阿汐在瓶堆里翻出一只小酒瓶，瓶身上画着一条胖鱼，是她六岁那年扔进泉州港的，里头一张纸：「爹快回来。」纸背面多了一行，墨色淡了：「收到了。爹。」她捧着瓶子坐了很久。识字的漂客说：「这湾里，只有这一封是回了信的。」

The archers withdraw. In the pile Axi turns up a little wine bottle with a fat fish painted on it: she threw it into Quanzhou harbour when she was six. Inside is a slip of paper: 'Father, come home soon.' On the back is one more line, the ink faded: 'Got it. Father.' She sits holding the bottle for a long time. 'Of everything in this bay,' says the castaway who reads, 'that's the only one that ever got an answer.'

name: 潮钟亭
Tide Bell Pavilion
before: 野地里一座小亭，亭里吊着一口铜钟，钟下一口石井，井底有暗沟通着海。漂客们说这钟从前会自己响，一天两回，后来就哑了。这几天一队亡骑围着小亭打转，拿枪杆一下下捅那口钟，捅得钟身直晃，就是不响，捅不响，他们也不走。

A small pavilion stands in the open with a bronze bell hanging inside it, and beneath the bell a stone shaft with a hidden channel running to the sea. The bell used to ring by itself twice a day, the castaways say, and then it went dumb. For days a troop of dead riders has circled the pavilion, jabbing the bell with their spear butts until it swings, but it never rings. It won't ring, and still they won't leave.
after: 亡骑散了。阿汐趴在井口看了看：井里一只木浮子连着钟锤，潮一涨，浮子上来，钟就响。暗沟口被海草塞死了，她下去掏了半个时辰。傍晚潮来，钟「当」地响了一声，满野的漂客都抬起了头。钟沿上刻着一行字：「留给不会看月亮的人。许。」

The riders scatter. Axi peers down the shaft: a wooden float inside is linked to the clapper, so when the tide rises the float lifts and the bell rings. The channel mouth is choked with weed, and she climbs down and digs for an hour. At dusk the tide comes in and the bell sounds once, clang, and every castaway across the fields looks up. Around its rim runs a line: 'For those who cannot read the moon. Xu.'

name: 潮杆岬
Tide Pole Point
before: 白沙路扫到了尽头：一道石岬伸进静水，岬尖立着一根潮杆，杆下两块平石，像两张凳子。岬上驻着一营守墟的精兵，三路排开，把潮杆围在当中。扫地的守墟人走到岬口，扫帚停了，第一次回头看你们，手腕上的铜铃轻轻响了一下。

The swept path ends at a stone point running out into the still water, with a tide pole at its tip and two flat stones beneath it like a pair of stools. A camp of picked Ruin-keepers holds the point, drawn up in three columns around the pole. At the neck of the point the sweeper stops his broom and, for the first time, turns to look at you. The bell at his wrist gives a soft ring.
after: 精兵退进了水里。潮杆上刻满了潮时，最后一行是：「八月十八大潮，礁门水深，可出。」杆底下埋着一只竹匣，匣里两只粗茶碗。岬下的渔家说，那几年每天傍晚，一个领港、一个马帮汉子坐在这两块石头上喝茶看潮；往东走那天，马帮汉子把铃拴在一个天天站在岬上看他们的守墟人手上：「替我们扫着路，后来的人好走。」扫地人把铃解下来，放进阿汐手里，扫帚靠在潮杆上，一步一步走进了水里，水面一圈涟漪都没有。阿汐握着铃：「能出去的。他们知道能出去，还是往东走了。」

The picked guards withdraw into the water. The pole is carved all over with tide times, and the last line reads: 'Eighth month, eighteenth day, spring tide. Deep water at the reef gate. A ship can leave.' Buried at its foot is a bamboo box holding two coarse tea bowls. Those years, say the fisherfolk below the point, a pilot and a caravan man sat on these stones every evening drinking tea and watching the tide. The day they left eastward, the caravan man tied his bell to the wrist of a keeper who stood on the point watching them every day. 'Keep the path swept for us. It'll be easier for whoever comes after.' The sweeper unties the bell and puts it in Axi's hand, leans his broom against the pole, and walks step by step into the water without a ripple. Axi closes her hand on the bell. 'They could have left. They knew they could, and they went east anyway.'

name: 夜戏台
Night Stage
before: 野地中间搭着一座戏台，台下黑压压坐着一大营守墟人：亡兵坐前排，亡弓坐后排，亡骑骑着马站在最后头。台上是一个漂来的戏班，十几个人，每晚都得唱，唱到天亮才许歇。班主嗓子早哑了，还在硬撑，小旦一边唱一边掉眼泪，台下没有一张脸，也没有一声好。

A stage stands in the middle of the open land, and below it sits a great camp of Ruin-keepers: soldiers in the front rows, archers behind, riders on horseback at the very back. On stage is a troupe of a dozen castaway players who must perform every night until dawn. The troupe master's voice went long ago and he is still forcing it out; the young lead weeps as she sings. Below the stage there is not a single face, and not a single cheer.
after: 守墟人散了，戏班子瘫在台上。班主说他们只肯听一出，叫《送潮》，是十年前千里号的人在这台上唱的：一伙人排成一行往东走，领港走在最后，回了三次头，唱一句「潮会带他们来」。「守墟人一回回地听，」班主说，「像是想把这出戏记住。」

The keepers disperse and the troupe collapses on the boards. There is only one piece they will listen to, the master says, called Seeing Off the Tide, first sung on this stage by the Qianli's people ten years ago: a company walks east in a line, the pilot last of all, looking back three times and singing, 'The tide will bring them here.' 'The keepers listen to it again and again,' says the master, 'as if they're trying to learn it by heart.'

name: 葫芦渡
Gourd Ferry
before: 海边一处渡口，对面就是南屿。渡船是几百只干葫芦捆成的筏子，浮得高，划得慢。撑筏的是个哑巴老汉，十年来只摆这一条水。一队亡兵蹲在渡口，拿枪尖把葫芦一只只戳破，戳破一只，筏子就往下沉一点，老汉蹲在旁边一只只地补。

A ferry landing on the coast, the South Islet just across the water. The ferry is a raft of hundreds of dried gourds lashed together, riding high and paddling slow. The ferryman is a mute old man who has worked this one crossing for ten years. A squad of dead soldiers squats at the landing, puncturing the gourds one by one with their spear points, and with each one the raft sinks a little lower while the old man crouches beside it patching them.
after: 亡兵退了，老汉补好最后一只葫芦，在沙上比画给你们看：一个黑脸汉子，夜里独自过渡去了南屿，怀里揣着一本簿子；天亮回来，手里空了。老汉竖起三根手指：那是他们往东走的前三天。他拍拍筏子，示意你们上来。

The soldiers withdraw. The old man patches the last gourd and sketches in the sand for you: a dark-faced man crossed to the South Islet alone one night, a book held against his chest; at dawn he came back empty-handed. The old man holds up three fingers: that was three days before they all went east. He pats the raft and beckons you aboard.

name: 头骡湾
Lead Mule Bay
before: 北边的海滩上，一群骡子站在静水里吃海草，吃得满嘴绿。它们是在这里生、在这里长的，没见过山。只有一头老白骡不吃，天天面朝西站着，背上还搭着一副磨烂的驮鞍。一队亡弓在沙丘上拿它当靶子，箭落在它蹄子边上，它四条腿像钉进了沙里，动也不动。

On the northern beach a herd of mules stands in the still water eating seaweed, mouths stained green. They were born and raised here and have never seen a mountain. Only one old white mule does not eat. Every day it stands facing west with a worn-out pack saddle still on its back. A squad of dead archers on the dunes uses it for target practice, arrows landing beside its hooves, but it stands as if its four legs were nailed into the sand.
after: 亡弓退了，老白骡还是朝西站着。驮鞍底下钉着一块木牌：「陆字号头骡」。小桨问头骡是什么，龚墨斗说是马帮里打头走的那一头，镖头自己骑。阿汐顺着骡子的眼睛往西望，那边是雪山的方向：「它在等陆九。」

The archers fall back and the old mule goes on facing west. A wooden tag is nailed under the saddle: 'Lu House, Lead Mule.' Xiaojiang asks what a lead mule is. The one at the head of the caravan, Gong Modou tells him, the one the chief rides himself. Axi follows the mule's gaze west, towards where the snow mountains lie. 'It's waiting for Lu Jiu.'

name: 茶渣岗
Tea Leaf Mound
before: 野地里一座小土岗，岗上的土是黑的，踩上去发软，走近了闻到一股陈茶味。一队亡弓守在岗顶，见人上岗就放箭，箭射进土里，一直没到箭羽。漂客们说这岗是十年里一点点堆起来的，没人知道是什么堆的，只知道守墟人不许人挖。

A low mound rises in the open, its earth black and soft underfoot, and close up it smells of old tea. A squad of dead archers holds the top and shoots at anyone who climbs it, arrows sinking into the soil up to their fletching. The castaways say the mound grew a little at a time over ten years. Nobody knows what it is made of, only that the keepers forbid digging.
after: 亡弓退了，你们往下挖了一尺，还是黑的：全是煮过的茶叶，一层压一层。龚墨斗捏了一把：「百来号人，喝上好几年，才堆得起这么高。」茶渣里埋着一口缺了耳的大铁锅，锅底铸着四个字：「陆家马帮」。马帮在这里住过，而且住了好几年。

The archers withdraw and you dig down a foot: still black, nothing but boiled tea leaves pressed layer on layer. Gong Modou squeezes a handful. 'A hundred-odd men drinking for years. That's what it takes to pile it this high.' Buried in the leaves is a great iron cauldron with a broken handle, cast on its base: 'Lu Family Caravan'. The caravan lived here, and for years.

name: 学舌岩
Parrot Crag
before: 海边一面石崖，崖上住着一群绿鹦鹉，吵得整片海滩都听得见。它们会说人话，说的不是泉州话，是一口山里的腔调，一只起头，满崖跟着喊。一队亡弓守在崖下，一箭一箭往崖上射，鹦鹉飞起来，落下去，接着喊。守墟人不喜欢吵，这面崖他们打了好几年了。

A rock face on the coast is home to a flock of green parrots so loud the whole beach can hear them. They talk, and not in the Quanzhou tongue but in a hill-country accent; one starts and the whole cliff takes it up. A squad of dead archers below shoots up at them arrow after arrow, and the parrots fly up, settle again, and keep shouting. The keepers dislike noise. They have been fighting this cliff for years.
after: 亡弓退了，鹦鹉们喊得更响了：「赶马哟——」「歇脚啰——」「镖头来了没？」「没来，再等等。」龚墨斗听出来，是茶路上的赶马调。这些鹦鹉是听着马帮的人说话长大的。马帮走了好些年，它们还在一遍遍地问：镖头来了没。

The archers withdraw and the parrots shout louder than ever. 'Drive the mules, hey!' 'Rest your feet, ho!' 'Has the chief come?' 'Not yet, wait a bit more.' Gong Modou recognises the muleteers' songs from the tea road. These birds grew up listening to the caravan men talk. The caravan left years ago, and still they ask, over and over: has the chief come yet?

name: 竹筏湾
Bamboo Raft Bay
before: 一道海湾里搁着几十张烂竹筏，竹子是山里的毛竹，归墟根本不长。三路守墟人在湾里扎了营，一张一张地拆筏子，拆下来的竹子码成一垛，又一根根扔进海里，扔完了再去拆下一张。漂客们说，这些筏子是很多年前从西边漂来的，筏上的人上了岸，筏子就一直搁在这儿。

Dozens of rotting bamboo rafts lie beached in a bay. The bamboo is the big mountain kind; nothing like it grows in the Ruins. Ruin-keepers in three columns have camped here, taking the rafts apart one by one, stacking the poles, then throwing them into the sea one at a time and moving on to the next raft. The rafts drifted in from the west many years ago, the castaways say. The people on them came ashore, and the rafts have lain here ever since.
after: 守墟人退进了水里。筏子上的藤结是马帮捆驮子的结法，龚墨斗一眼就认了出来。最大的一张筏子，横木上刻着一行字：「江尽处是海，海尽处是墟。镖头守着崖上的路，没有来。」马帮是扎了筏子顺江漂下来的，陆九没有跟来。

The keepers withdraw into the water. The rattan knots on the rafts are the knots muleteers use to lash their loads; Gong Modou knows them at a glance. On a crossbeam of the largest raft a line is carved: 'Where the river ends, the sea; where the sea ends, the Ruins. The chief stayed to guard the cliff road. He did not come.' The caravan came down the river on rafts. Lu Jiu did not come with them.

name: 无叶茶寮
Leafless Teahouse
before: 路口一间茶寮，每天正午，一队亡兵排着队进来，每人领一碗茶，端着站一会儿，再整碗倒在地上，转身出去。茶寮的瓦罐叔给他们倒了好些年，不敢不倒。今天亡兵不排队了，进门就来搬茶炉，瓦罐叔抱着茶壶缩在柜台后头，直喊「炉子搬走了，明天拿什么倒」。

There is a teahouse at the crossroads. Every day at noon a squad of dead soldiers files in, each takes a bowl of tea, holds it a while, then pours the whole bowl on the floor and walks out. Uncle Wapan has poured for them for years and never dared refuse. Today the soldiers do not queue; they come straight in to carry off the stove, and Uncle Wapan cowers behind the counter clutching his teapot, wailing, 'Take the stove and what do I pour tomorrow?'
after: 亡兵被打散，瓦罐叔给你们一人倒了一碗，茶汤清亮，香得很。你们问是什么茶，他揭开壶盖给你们看：里头一片叶子都没有。「是东边那口井的水，打上来就是这个味儿。马帮的人挖的井。」

The soldiers are scattered and Uncle Wapan pours you each a bowl, clear and fragrant. When you ask what tea it is, he lifts the lid to show you: not a single leaf inside. 'It's water from the well to the east. Comes up tasting like this. The caravan men dug it.'

name: 破船寨
Wreck Stockade
before: 海边礁上卡着一条破海船，船头朝天，船身裂成了两半。船上下来的海盗就在礁下扎了寨，三路排开，刀手、弓手，还有骑着抢来骡子的。他们是冲着「千里号满仓的普洱」来的，听说一块茶砖换一块金，进了归墟才发觉出不去，就在岸上到处挖，挖地三尺。

A broken seagoing ship is wedged on the reef, bow to the sky, hull split in two. The pirates who came off it have built a stockade below the reef, drawn up in three columns: blades, bows, and riders on stolen mules. They came for 'the Qianli's holds full of Pu'er', a gold bar for every tea brick, they heard, and only once inside the Ruins did they find they couldn't get out. Now they dig everywhere ashore, three feet down.
after: 这一伙海盗被打散了，有的跪下来求你们带他们出去。可这道礁是归墟的门槛，每隔几个月就有一条做发财梦的船撞上来，船碎了，人上了岸，寨子又会满。漂客们说，清一回，能安生一阵子。他们挖出来的只有一块茶砖，砖上印着「陆」，早泡成了泥。

This gang is broken, and some kneel and beg you to take them out with you. But this reef is the threshold of the Ruins: every few months another ship full of dreams of fortune runs onto it, the ship breaks, the men come ashore, and the stockade fills up again. Clear it once, the castaways say, and you get some peace for a while. All the pirates ever dug up was one tea brick stamped Lu, long since soaked to mud.

name: 红树市
Mangrove Market
before: 沼泽里一片红树林，林子当中十几座木屋吊在树杈上，一条条栈板连着，这就是红树市。市主是个独腿的番商，大胡子，船沉了，他没沉，就在树上开了铺。可这几天一队亡骑踩着烂泥在栈板底下转来转去，谁上栈板就把板子掀翻，番商在树上骂了三天，嗓子都骂哑了。

In a mangrove forest in the marsh a dozen wooden huts hang in the branches, linked by plank walkways: the Mangrove Market. Its master is a one-legged foreign trader with a great beard. His ship sank; he didn't, and he opened shop up in the trees. But for days a troop of dead riders has been churning the mud beneath the walkways, overturning the planks under anyone who steps on them, and the trader has been cursing from his tree for three days until his voice is gone.
after: 亡骑退了，番商从树上吊下一只篮子，佩服你们，愿意拿沉船里捞来的货跟你们换。他说马帮的人在他这儿买过东西：铺子里所有的大陶罐，一只不剩。「他们拿罐子装井里的茶水，说往东全是海，海上喝不着茶。」

The riders withdraw. The trader lowers a basket from his tree, impressed with you, and offers goods salvaged from wrecks in trade. The caravan men bought from him once, he says: every big clay jar in his shop, down to the last. 'They filled them with tea water from the well. Said east of here it's all sea, and you can't get tea at sea.'

name: 蹄铁榕
Horseshoe Banyan
before: 海边一棵老榕树，树干上钉满了骡蹄铁，一圈压一圈，锈成了红褐色。一伙亡弓拿刀把蹄铁一只只撬下来，磨成箭头：归墟不出铁，铁比什么都金贵。树下一个漂客老汉跪着求他们留几只：「这是人家的记号！」

An old banyan on the coast has its trunk studded with mule shoes, ring upon ring, rusted red-brown. A band of dead archers is prising them off one by one with knives to grind into arrowheads: the Ruins yield no iron, and iron is worth more than anything. An old castaway kneels at the foot of the tree begging them to leave a few. 'Those are somebody's markers!'
after: 亡弓被赶走，蹄铁一只只钉了回去。老汉说马帮的规矩，骡子死在路上，就把它的蹄铁钉在路边的树上。可这棵树上的蹄铁大半没磨过，是新掌。马帮往东走那天，把骡子全留下了，掌一齐卸下来钉在树上：「海上用不着骡子，骡子留给后来的人。」

The archers are driven off and the shoes go back up one by one. Caravan custom, the old man says: when a mule dies on the road, you nail its shoes to a tree by the way. But most of these shoes were never worn; they are new. The day the caravan went east, they left all their mules behind, took off their shoes and nailed them here together. 'No use for mules at sea. Leave the mules for whoever comes after.'

name: 赛骡场
Mule Racecourse
before: 野地里一圈跑道，是漂客家的孩子拿石子摆出来的，每年秋天在这儿赛骡子，赢了的喝一碗井里的茶。今年比到一半，一队亡骑闯进了跑道，跟着骡子一起跑，跑得比谁都快，孩子们吓得从骡背上滚了下来，骡子倒是不怕，撒开蹄子追了上去。

A racetrack laid out with pebbles in the open: the castaways' children race mules here every autumn, and the winner drinks a bowl of tea from the well. Halfway through this year's race a troop of dead riders burst onto the track and galloped along with the mules, faster than any of them. The children tumbled off in fright. The mules were not frightened at all, and set off after them.
after: 亡骑被赶出了跑道，孩子们又爬上骡背。领头的大孩子说，这场赛是马帮兴起来的：那年马帮要往东去，守墟人不放，马帮的头领就跟守墟人的骑兵赛了一场，拿路作注，骡子赢了马。「所以守墟人每年都来，」孩子说，「他们想赢回去。」

The riders are chased off the track and the children climb back on. The race was started by the caravan, the eldest says: the year the caravan wanted to go east, the keepers wouldn't let them, so the caravan's leader raced the keepers' cavalry with the road as the stake, and the mules beat the horses. 'That's why the keepers come every year,' the boy says. 'They want to win it back.'

name: 等茶石
Waiting Stone
before: 白沙路拐过一片矮林，路边一块平顶石，石上摆着一只粗碗。扫地的守墟人扫到这里停下，从腰间解下一只竹筒，往碗里倒满茶，站一会儿，再把茶泼在石头脚下。一队亡骑从林子里冲出来要掀了这块石头，扫地人不躲也不拦，只伸手护着那只碗。

The swept path rounds a stand of scrub to a flat-topped stone by the wayside with a coarse bowl on it. Here the sweeper stops, unties a bamboo flask from his belt, fills the bowl with tea, stands a moment, then pours it out at the foot of the stone. A troop of dead riders charges out of the scrub to overturn the stone. The sweeper neither dodges nor blocks them; he only shields the bowl with his hand.
after: 亡骑被打散。石头上刻着一行歪歪扭扭的字：「老十七在此等许领港喝茶，每日酉时。」漂客们说老十七是马帮里赶第十七头骡子的，嗓门大，跟那个看潮的领港最要好。扫地人收起碗，接着往前扫，路朝岬角那边去了。

The riders are scattered. A crooked line is carved into the stone: 'Old Seventeen waits here to drink tea with Pilot Xu. Every day at the hour of the rooster.' Old Seventeen, the castaways say, drove the seventeenth mule in the caravan, a man with a big voice and the tide-watching pilot's best friend. The sweeper picks up his bowl and sweeps on. The path heads for the point.

name: 蚂蟥塘
Leech Pond
before: 沼泽里一片死水塘，水黑得发亮，蚂蟥一伸一缩地游。一队亡兵站在塘里，水没到腰，一动不动，蚂蟥爬满了他们的腿也不掉：他们身上没有血，蚂蟥白爬。他们守着塘中间一座小土墩，墩上插着一根竹竿，竿头挂着一只布袋。

A pond of dead water in the marsh, black and glossy, leeches stretching and bunching as they swim. A squad of dead soldiers stands in it waist-deep, motionless, leeches crawling all over their legs and never dropping off: there is no blood in them, so the leeches crawl for nothing. They guard a little mound in the middle with a bamboo pole stuck in it and a cloth bag hanging from the top.
after: 亡兵被赶出了塘，你们扎紧裤腿，腿上抹了盐蹚过去。布袋里是一包烟丝和一张字条，马帮的字：「过蚂蟥塘，腿上抹盐，烟油一点它就掉。给镖头留的，他怕这东西。」名震茶路的陆九，原来怕蚂蟥。

The soldiers are driven out of the pond, and you bind your trouser legs, rub salt on your shins and wade across. In the bag is a twist of tobacco and a note in caravan script: 'Crossing Leech Pond: salt on your legs, and a dab of tobacco juice makes them drop off. Left for the chief. He's scared of these.' Lu Jiu, the terror of the tea road, is afraid of leeches.

name: 喊爹礁
Calling Reef
before: 海边一道长礁，每天傍晚，一个八九岁的男孩站在礁头，朝东喊「爹——」，喊满一百声才回家。一队亡骑嫌他吵，天天来把他从礁上赶下去，他娘追在后面，一手拉孩子，一手拿扫帚打马腿。男孩边跑边回头喊：「还差三十七声！」

Every evening an eight- or nine-year-old boy stands at the end of a long reef on the coast and shouts 'Father!' eastwards, a hundred times, before he goes home. A troop of dead riders finds him too noisy and comes every day to chase him off the reef, his mother running after them, dragging her son with one hand and whacking the horses' legs with a broom in the other. The boy looks back as he runs. 'Thirty-seven more to go!'
after: 亡骑被打跑，男孩把剩下的三十七声喊完了。他娘说孩子他爹是马帮的人，那几年在归墟成了家，往东走的时候说：「等镖头到了，我就回来。」孩子长这么大没见过山，可沙滩上画的全是山，一座比一座高。「他爹说，山上有雪，」她说，「孩子不信，雪怎么会是白的。」

The riders are driven off and the boy finishes his last thirty-seven shouts. His father was a caravan man, his mother says, who made a home in the Ruins in those years. When he went east he said, 'When the chief gets here, I'll come back.' The boy has never seen a mountain, but everything he draws in the sand is mountains, each taller than the last. 'His father told him there's snow on mountains,' she says. 'He won't believe snow can be white.'

name: 茶井集
Tea Well Market
before: 野地当中一口井，井台是整块的青石，井边围着一圈摊子，是归墟的漂客们唯一的集市：换鱼的、卖椰子的、修鞋的，都靠这口井的水过日子。可如今井台上站着一队亡弓，弓都拉满了，谁放下桶就射谁的桶。漂客们说，守墟人以前从不管这口井，自从海上亮起了后千里的灯，他们就把井围了起来。

A well in the middle of the open land, its curb a single slab of bluestone, ringed by stalls: the only market in the Ruins. Fish traders, coconut sellers, cobblers, all live off this well's water. But now a squad of dead archers stands on the curb, bows drawn, and shoots the bucket of anyone who lowers one. The keepers never used to care about the well, the castaways say. Only since Houqianli's lanterns lit up out at sea have they ringed it.
after: 亡弓退了，第一桶水打上来，清得照得见人，喝一口，满嘴茶香，还回甘。漂客们把摊子重新支起来，粮食换金子的买卖开了张。井台上刻着马帮的字：「挖井三月，人人投茶一块。茶在，路在。镖头未至，留茶一口，候之。」井沿上压着一只扣着盖的碗，揭开一看，碗里的茶十年没干，还是温的。

The archers withdraw and the first bucket comes up clear enough to see your face in. One mouthful tastes of tea, with a sweet finish. The castaways set their stalls up again, and grain-for-gold trade opens. On the curb the caravan carved: 'Three months digging. Each man dropped in a piece of tea. While the tea lasts, the road lasts. The chief has not come. One mouthful of tea is left for him.' A lidded bowl is weighted on the rim. Lift the lid: the tea in it has not dried in ten years, and it is still warm.

name: 茶味税卡
Tea Tax Post
before: 去茶井的路上横着一道木卡，卡上挂着牌子：「茶味税，每碗一文」。收税的是个穿破官袍的漂客，自称朝廷委任的「归墟茶课大使」，手里一方大印，盖谁谁就得交钱。他雇了一队亡骑守卡，那些亡骑听不懂，他说一句，它们就站一会儿，倒也唬人。

A wooden barrier crosses the road to the well with a sign: 'Tea Flavour Tax, one copper a bowl.' The collector is a castaway in a ragged official robe who calls himself the Court-Appointed Tea Commissioner of the Ruins, with a great seal in his hand; whoever he stamps must pay. He has a troop of dead riders guarding the post. They can't understand a word, but every time he speaks they stand there a moment, and it looks impressive enough.
after: 亡骑散了，「茶课大使」交出了大印。龚墨斗翻过来一看，哪是官印，是一块砖模：马帮压茶砖用的，刻着「普洱·千里号贡·丁未」。茶砖是贡茶，可这一路上没有朝廷，贡给谁？大使挠挠头：「我捡到的时候，就想当个官。」

The riders scatter and the 'Tea Commissioner' hands over his seal. Gong Modou turns it over: no official seal at all, but a brick mould the caravan used for pressing tea, carved 'Pu'er. Tribute of the Qianli. Dingwei.' The bricks were tribute tea. But there is no court out here. Tribute to whom? The commissioner scratches his head. 'When I found it, I just fancied being an official.'

name: 火塘屋
Hearth House
before: 野地里一座长屋，是马帮当年住的，屋当中一口火塘，火一直没灭，一个漂客寡妇天天往里添椰壳。一队亡骑围着长屋转，守墟人见不得火，转一圈，往门里扔一把沙。寡妇拿身子挡在火塘前，沙落了她一头一脸，她还在添。

A longhouse stands in the open where the caravan once lived. In the middle burns a hearth that has never gone out; a castaway widow feeds it coconut husks every day. A troop of dead riders circles the house, for the keepers cannot abide fire; with every lap they fling a handful of sand through the door. The widow shields the hearth with her body, sand all over her head and face, and keeps on feeding it.
after: 亡骑被赶走，寡妇抖了抖头上的沙。火塘上方的大梁上刻着马帮的花名册，一个名字一道勾，勾的意思是「往东了」。只有两行没勾：一行是「镖头陆九」；一行没有名字，只写着「跑信的」，旁边一行小字，像是谁随手添的：「又晚了。」

The riders are driven off and the widow shakes the sand from her hair. Carved on the great beam above the hearth is the caravan's roster, a tick beside each name, and a tick means 'gone east'. Only two lines have no tick. One reads 'Chief Lu Jiu'. The other has no name at all, only 'the runner', and beside it, as if someone added it in passing: 'Late again.'
